newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says forex moves rather sharp, watching effect.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says forex moves rather sharp, watching effect.

text.p: The pace of recent movements in the currency markets has been rather sharp and the Bank of Japan will continue to watch their effect on the domestic economy, BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a news conference on Wednesday.
"The pace of recent developments in the currency markets has been rather fast and we will continue to watch the effects on the economy closely," he said.
Although Matsushita declined to comment when asked if he thought the yen was too weak, he said it was desirable for exchange rates to reflect economic fundamentals and to move in a moderate fashion.

Asked whether the BOJ was concerned about possible linkage between the fall in the yen and that of stock prices, Matsushita said: "At the moment there seems to be no need to worry about such a linkage."
The BOJ governor also declined to comment on the level of Tokyo share prices, but said the central bank was keeping a close watch on their movement.
But he said the recent fall in stock prices was one reason for the sluggishness of corporate sentiment.
"The recent fall in stock prices is one reason businesses can't shrug off concerns about the future of the economy," he said.
Matsushita also said that the drop in stocks may affect private consumption and added that the central bank would continue to monitor the effects and the factors behind the fall closely.
Asked whether the fall in stocks would hurt the profits of financial institutions, Matsushita said:
"We cannot ignore the effect on the bad loans problems of individual institutions and their earnings results."
Asked about the movement in long-term interest rates, Matsushita said they were decided by many factors and market participants' outlook on the economy was one big factor.
